objective.statement: Split the 900-line checkout handler in src/checkout/handler.ts into smaller modules as a pure refactor, preserving every public export and keeping every existing test green.
objective.success_definition: src/checkout/handler.ts is decomposed into smaller modules; every public export is preserved; the entire existing test suite passes; no behaviour has changed.

goals.statement: Split the 900-line checkout handler in src/checkout/handler.ts into smaller modules.
acceptance: The handler's logic is distributed across multiple smaller modules instead of one 900-line file.

goals.statement: Keep every public export of the handler.
acceptance: Every public export present before the refactor is still exported afterwards under the same name.
The full existing test suite passes after the refactor.

goals.statement: Do not change behaviour; the change is a pure refactor.
acceptance: Only code organization changes; observable behaviour is identical before and after.

constraints.statement: Do not change behaviour — pure refactor only.
Every public export of src/checkout/handler.ts must be preserved.
Every existing test must remain green.

non_goals.statement: Changing behaviour of the checkout handler.
Adding new features or functionality; the work is a pure refactor.

include: The new smaller modules created by splitting src/checkout/handler.ts

assumptions.statement: The new smaller modules will live under src/checkout/, alongside the original handler.
"Keep every existing test green" means the current test suite passes unmodified after the refactor.
The repository has a runnable existing test suite that exercises the checkout handler.
The public export surface to preserve is exactly what src/checkout/handler.ts currently exports.
The specific module boundaries and file names for the split are left to the implementer's judgment.

open_questions.question: How should the handler be decomposed — what module boundaries and names should the split use?
options: Split by responsibility (e.g., validation, pricing, payment, persistence)
Split by extracting cohesive groups of related functions
Leave the decomposition to the implementer

open_questions.question: Where should the new module files live?
options: In a new subdirectory under src/checkout/

verification.spec: Run the repository's existing test suite using the project's standard test command.
Compare the public export surface of src/checkout/handler.ts before and after the split.
verification.expected: The set of public exports is identical.

verification.spec: Review the diff to confirm it consists only of code movement and reorganization into smaller modules, with no logic edits.
verification.expected: The diff shows pure code motion; no behavioural changes.

deliverables.description: src/checkout/handler.ts split into smaller modules with the public export surface unchanged and all existing tests passing.

factors: The file is ~900 lines, a large surface for accidental behaviour drift during code motion.
Preserving the exact public export surface while moving code into new modules risks missed or renamed exports.
The existing test suite is the only stated safety net for detecting behaviour changes.
